question: Ryff Well-Being Framework
content: Carol Ryff identified Purpose in Life as one of the six fundamental pillars of psychological well-being.
description: Your psychology textbook mentions a well-being framework with six pillars including Purpose in Life. Which researcher developed this framework?
explanation: Ryff model includes self-acceptance, positive relations, autonomy, environmental mastery, personal growth, and purpose in life.

question: Gene Expression and Purpose
content: Steven Cole UCLA research showed eudaimonic well-being correlates with down-regulation of pro-inflammatory genes and up-regulation of antiviral response genes.
description: Research shows purpose-driven individuals have lower inflammation and stronger antiviral defenses at the genetic level. Which scientist work aligns with this?
explanation: Cole research demonstrates purpose acts as an epigenetic dimmer switch on gene expression.

question: Epigenetic Dimmer Switch
content: Purpose acts as an epigenetic dimmer switch turning down pro-inflammatory gene expression and turning up antiviral responses.
description: Your biology professor describes a psychological factor that can turn down inflammatory gene expression. What metaphor does the course use?
explanation: Purpose is described as an epigenetic dimmer switch modulating inflammatory and antiviral gene expression.

question: Diurnal Cortisol Curve
content: High purpose correlates with a healthy diurnal cortisol curve that peaks after waking and tapers off while low purpose leads to flattened dysregulated patterns.
description: Your patient has a flattened cortisol curve, chronic exhaustion, and insulin resistance. Which psychological factor is most relevant to investigate?
explanation: Purpose correlates with healthier cortisol regulation. A flattened curve is associated with low purpose.

question: Neurological Resilience
content: Purpose-driven individuals show greater gray matter volume in the insula and prefrontal cortex with rapid amygdala recovery after stress.
description: Brain scans show some participants amygdalae recover quickly from stress while others stay activated. What factor correlates with faster recovery?
explanation: Purpose-driven brains show rapid amygdala recovery via prefrontal cortex regulation of threat detection.

question: Cognitive Reserve
content: High purpose reduces all-cause mortality by over 20% and heart attack risk by up to 50% while providing cognitive reserve against decline.
description: An autopsy reveals Alzheimer plaques in an elderly brain yet the patient showed no cognitive decline in life. What concept explains this?
explanation: High-purpose individuals demonstrate cognitive reserve maintaining function despite brain pathology.

question: Longitudinal Evidence
content: The Rush Memory and Aging Project shows purpose-in-life scores predict reduced stroke, heart attack, and all-cause mortality.
description: Which longitudinal study provides the strongest evidence that purpose reduces all-cause mortality and heart attack risk?
explanation: The Rush Memory and Aging Project tracked purpose-in-life scores and found dramatic reductions in mortality, stroke, and heart attack risk.
